referenceSources.title: Record-breaking Rover goes under the hammer | cars4starters
referenceSources.description:
This yellow and white Rover 220 Coupe Turbo, known as the ‘Tomcat’, is presented in its original land speed record–breaking specification. The side profile showcases sponsor decals from Texaco, Harman/Kardon, Michelin Pilot, MEB TRW Steering & Suspension Systems, and Garrett Turbo, along with alloy wheels and a rear spoiler. Stripped to a bare shell and rebuilt with engine performance enhancements, a roll cage, racing seat, and large-capacity fuel tank, the coupe achieved 37 UK land speed records in 1992, including a 24-hour endurance record of 138 mph and a flying 5 km run at 156 mph.

One of two specially modified pre-production prototypes, this sole survivor remains in its record-setting form. Auctioned at Millbrook Proving Ground in Bedfordshire, it still holds 36 of its records and was recommissioned in 2002 for a commemorative event. The car’s bold livery and motorsport upgrades reflect its historic achievement as the fastest production-based 2.0-litre front-wheel-drive vehicle of its era.
